topic: Auto rotation, ground resonance, vertex ring, blade sailing
syllabus_extract: Auto rotation, ground resonance, vertex ring, blade sailing.
specific_objectives: 13.1.1.1 Trainee will be able to explain the helicopter control, main rotor movements, translation flight, power, auto rotation, vibration checks and various adjustments.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Review of IB diagrams regarding rotor dynamics; Instructor supervision of theoretical explanation only.
intro_questions: What is the primary function of the main rotor in translation flight?
Define the term 'auto rotation' in the context of engine failure.
List two common causes of excessive vibration in the rotor system.

development.content:
Auto rotation entry and control
Main rotor behavior during descent
Power management in auto rotation
Vibration checks and adjustments

Ground resonance mechanism
Vertex ring identification
Blade sailing characteristics
Safety implications of resonance

Remedial actions for vibration
Monitoring device indications
Preventive maintenance checks
Reporting procedures for anomalies

summary_questions: Explain the difference between ground resonance and blade sailing.
Describe the immediate pilot actions required upon entering auto rotation.
How does the vertex ring assist in diagnosing rotor imbalance?
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note on the remedial actions for gearbox vibrators as covered in the next lesson plan (LP 09) to bridge the gap between rotor dynamics and monitoring devices.

pft_rows.syllabus: Vibration of rotor and gearbox vibrators, disc cause effects on helicopter monitoring devices and remedial action. On hand experience to use vibration measuring equipment’s.
pft_rows.references: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
